subject.title: [Regression]: sessions_spawn missing scope operator.write — introduced between v2026.6.1 and v2026.6.11

question: Should in-process `callSubagentGateway` dispatch use a synthetic operator client with `operator.write` for non-admin `agent` calls after `sessions_spawn` tool policy has allowed the spawn?
rationale: The likely fix restores multi-agent delegation but deliberately changes the internal authorization boundary from inheriting a channel/plugin caller client to using synthetic operator write scope.

options.title: Confirm Synthetic Write Boundary
options.body: Land or refine the current narrow PR after redacted real token-auth `sessions_spawn` proof confirms the behavior and admin-only cleanup remains admin-scoped.

options.title: Keep Caller-Client Inheritance
options.body: Reject synthetic write elevation and instead require the channel/runtime client construction path to carry `operator.write` where delegation is allowed.

options.title: Pause For Broader Gateway Auth Policy
options.body: Treat this issue as part of the wider token/device-identity cluster and resolve it through a broader Gateway auth design before landing the narrow PR.

recommendation.title: Confirm Synthetic Write Boundary
recommendation.body: Land or refine the current narrow PR after redacted real token-auth `sessions_spawn` proof confirms the behavior and admin-only cleanup remains admin-scoped.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the in-process dispatch feature and is the strongest available owner for the security-boundary choice around that path.
